_comment: Articles that are not worth summarizing, with the reason. Not every Making Magic column carries an argument: some are link roundups, some are card-by-card preview galleries, some are mailbags with no through-line. Condensing those produces a page that says nothing. discover.mjs marks these 'skipped' so they stop surfacing at the top of the queue. Remove an id here to put it back in play.

ids.lets-talk-color-pie: Link index. A directory of every colour pie article and podcast Rosewater has made, with no argument of its own. The substance lives in the linked pieces — mechanical-color-pie-2021 is the one worth summarizing.
ids.celebrity: Personal essay about being famous — Phil Hartman, Clint Eastwood, Jim Henson, a Make-a-Wish visit. Rosewater's own genre label, and the column is about how to conduct yourself as a public face rather than about making anything. The one transferable idea (people connect to people, not ideas, so give the thing a human face) is a single aside. Kept the line at: does the article teach something about making things or receiving them, or about being a person? This is the third.
ids.new-new-world-order-2013-04-01: April Fools' hoax, published 1 April 2013 and signed off with "may you be careful reading articles on April Fools' Day." It invents an escalation of New World Order — square power/toughness, no instants at common, an eleven-word limit — that R&D never adopted. Summarizing it would state made-up rules as real design policy. new-world-order-2011-12-05 is the genuine article.
ids.out-of-the-closet-part-1: Personal column counting down Rosewater’s twenty favourite Magic T-shirts, published 10 July 2011. Design content is incidental biography (Tempest was his first lead, Squirrel Farm is his favourite card) and is covered properly by my-early-magic-years-part-1. Same call as celebrity: about being a person, not about making things. Note: part 2 is NOT skipped. Part 1 drew a badly split reaction, so Rosewater rewrote part 2 to attach an explicit design lesson to every shirt — traps in draft, cycling's debut, the Un- sets, guild self-identification. It is a design column wearing the first column's format.
ids.live-like-a-gamer: Self-help column from 8 December 2013: ten life lessons drawn from gaming (There’s a Solution, Prioritize, Trust the Math, Let People Do You Favors). Opens by stating the goal outright — “advice about how to make your life better.” The intended output is a better life, not better design. Same line as celebrity and the out-of-the-closet pair.
ids.ten-stories-tall: Lore recap and card gallery. Walks through the ten fairy tales behind Wilds of Eldraine's ten draft archetypes, plot by plot, listing which cards depict each. Thirty-eight short story paragraphs and hundreds of card names, with exactly one design sentence — the intro noting they attached a story to each two-colour archetype. That idea is already carried by city-highlights-part-2 (flavour the groupings so people assemble them instinctively) and the Wilds of Eldraine handoff pair. Nothing left to distil.
ids.one-thousand-two-hundred-and-counting: Index of the previous hundred columns, published 24 February 2025 at the 1,200-week mark — the latest in a recap series Rosewater has run every hundred articles since 2003. One short synopsis and a letter grade per article, with a link. He states its purpose outright: a record for finding a particular article, and a starting point for new readers. The design content is all pointers to other columns, most of which are separately in this archive or in the queue. Nothing to distil.
ids.trivial-pursuit-more-or-less: Counting quiz, published 24 June 2024. Each question gives two categories and asks which is larger; each answer is the enumerated list — nine expansions starting with S against seven starting with M, sixteen affinity variants against eleven landwalk variants, eleven 12/12s against seven 11/11s, ten steps in a turn against seven zones. The asides are historical facts rather than arguments. Note the contrast with trivial-pursuit-whats-in-a-name, which is summarized: that one's answers carry a real seam of naming craft (art and name colliding, exhausted naming space, codename policy). This one has nothing under the counts.
ids.one-thousand-one-hundred-and-counting: Index of the previous hundred columns, published 27 February 2023 at the 1,100-week mark. Same format and same series as one-thousand-two-hundred-and-counting, which is already skipped: a one-paragraph synopsis and a star rating per article, with a link, and the purpose stated outright — a record for finding a particular column, and a starting point for new readers. The design content is pointers to other columns, most of which are separately in this archive or in the queue. One real aside is why so few columns rate low (a constant scale across every recap article, rewriting anything under three stars, and twenty years of practice), but that is three sentences inside an index. Same call as the 1,200 column.
ids.addressing-magic-players-community-conce: Not a design column and not a Making Magic essay — a four-paragraph corporate statement published 14 March 2014 after Grand Prix Richmond, announcing that the judge Investigation Committee reviewed an attendee's conduct and that Wizards acted on its recommendation, and restating the Code of Conduct. Institutional voice throughout ("Wizards of the Coast is committed to…"); the scaffold's Rosewater byline is the fetch default, not a real one. There is no craft content of any kind to distil — no argument about making things or receiving them. It sits on the same news feed as the column, which is why the queue picked it up.
ids.magic-online-program-update-2012-mocs-ch: Organized Play announcement, published 7 March 2013 — not a design column and not by Rosewater. It lists the sixteen 2012 Magic Online Championship finalists by username, the formats and prize pool for the PAX East final, which Pro Tour each MOCS qualifier season now feeds into, plus Grand Prix Trials and promo codes. Programme news throughout, with no argument about making anything. Same category as the GP Richmond statement: it sits on the same news feed as the column, which is why the queue picked it up.
ids.one-two-three-times-murder-sideboarding-: A different column by a different author, published 5 September 2013 — part two of a strategy series on sideboarding, in Mike Flores's voice ("Thoughtcast was the glue that peanut buttered together the greatest offensive deck in the history of Magic"). It is about playing well: effective versus printed mana cost, why Deathmark outperformed Murder, colour-specific sideboard slots. Every one of the 242 articles in this archive is Rosewater's Making Magic; this is strategy content that shares the news feed. Third of this kind in a row, after the GP Richmond statement and the Magic Online programme update — expect more in this stretch of the queue.
ids.unfinity-and-beyond-2021-11-29: Duplicate of unfinity-and-beyond-2022-09-19, already summarized. The 2021 URL now serves the republished 2022 text verbatim, carrying the editor's note that the article originally ran 29 November 2021 and was re-run for Unfinity previews. Both dates therefore sit in the queue for one article; the archive keeps the 2022 slug because its JSON-LD date and slug agree.
ids.how-trivial-vampires-2021-10-25: Trivia quiz, published 25 October 2021: thirty multiple-choice questions about the Vampires of Magic, ahead of Crimson Vow previews. Every answer is an enumeration — the four Vampires printed before Odyssey, the seven Vampires with multiple legendary cards, the 271 Vampires available in white-black-red, the 57 Vampire cards with 'blood' in the name, and repeated 'there are no Vampires with devour yet'. Same profile as the already-skipped trivial-pursuit-more-or-less; unlike trivial-pursuit-whats-in-a-name and trivial-pursuit-all-innistrad, which are summarized because their answers carry craft. The one design fact here — Crovax needed the text 'counts as a Vampire' because Legend was a creature type and creatures had only one — is a single historical note, and the creature-type history is already covered in which-came-first-2022-03-14.
ids.one-thousand-and-counting-2021-02-22: Index of the previous hundred columns, published 23 February 2021 at the 1,000-week mark - the tenth instalment of the recurring recap series. The body is a numbered list of weeks #901-#1000, each with a one-sentence description of what that column covered and a one-to-five star rating; the only running prose is Rosewater's note on why few columns score low (a constant scale across all ten recaps, rewriting anything that falls below three stars, and improvement over nineteen years). No design argument of its own - the entries point at arguments made elsewhere, most of which are already summarized here. Same profile and same treatment as the already-skipped one-thousand-one-hundred-and-counting and one-thousand-two-hundred-and-counting.
ids.how-trivial-legendary-creatures-2020-11-: Trivia quiz, published 23 November 2020: thirty multiple-choice questions about legendary creatures, timed to Commander Legends. Judged by the same test applied to the other trivia columns - do the answers carry design argument? Here most do not. The bulk are lore identification (which plane a character is from, which gods are twins) and card-list enumeration (every card whose title names Ulamog). A handful of answers do carry something: Isamaru was designed on the spot to disprove a claim that no vanilla legendary could excite players; Atogatog got a design because art had already been commissioned for the cancelled Unglued 2; a rare poll run with the placeholder name Count Dracula changed how names are chosen before polling. Those three are each already covered - by act-of-war-part-1 (prove a risky idea with a working prototype), and by state-of-design-2022 and strixhaven-vision-design-handoff-document-part-1 on working titles going public. Not enough independent argument to reach seven lessons. Same treatment as how-trivial-vampires-2021-10-25 and trivial-pursuit-more-or-less; unlike trivial-pursuit-whats-in-a-name and trivial-pursuit-all-innistrad, which are summarized because their answers carry craft throughout.
ids.trivial-pursuit-2020-03-23: Trivia quiz, published 23 March 2020: thirty multiple-choice questions, one for each of thirty projects Rosewater led or co-led, a follow-up to the popular 25th-anniversary trivia column. Judged by the same test applied to the other trivia columns - do the answers carry design argument? Most do not. The bulk are card-list enumeration (how many cards with scry in Theros, how many legendary lands in Dominaria, which Ravnica Allegiance cards make Soldier tokens), debut identification (which set first printed Pacifism, which introduced the word create), and art or in-joke anecdotes (the earrings on B.F.M., the Vanguard life-total numbers, whether the Surgeon General likes teatime). About five answers carry something real: Aaron Forsythe was put on the Fifth Dawn design team to write an article about it, designed scry and sunburst, and was hired into R&D; Tom LaPille brought double-faced cards to Innistrad from Duel Masters, the Japan-only game allowed to push harder; Rosewater asked for Ixalan's two-sided conflict to become three-sided, with a fourth tribe added on need; the Scars block escalated its Phyrexian share from a minority to 50% to 90% across three sets; and convoke, built by Richard Garfield for the Boros, was moved to the Selesnya because it fit better. Of those, the punch-card and rehoming answers are already covered - by stepping-into-the-ring-part-1 (a physical accessory sets the frequency budget) and a-double-take-part-2 (rehome a rejected idea immediately). That leaves roughly three usable arguments, short of the seven a summary needs. Same treatment as how-trivial-legendary-creatures-2020-11-23, how-trivial-vampires-2021-10-25 and trivial-pursuit-more-or-less; unlike trivial-pursuit-whats-in-a-name and trivial-pursuit-all-innistrad, which are summarized because their answers carry craft throughout.
ids.nine-hundred-and-counting-2019-06-03: Index of the previous hundred columns, published 3 June 2019 at the 900-week mark - the ninth instalment of the recurring recap series, and Rosewater states its purpose outright: a record for finding a particular article, and a starting point for newer readers. The body is a numbered list of weeks #801-#900, each with a one-line description and a one-to-five star rating, plus a link. The design content is all pointers to other columns, most of which are separately in this archive or in the queue. Same profile and same treatment as the already-skipped one-thousand-and-counting-2021-02-22, one-thousand-one-hundred-and-counting and one-thousand-two-hundred-and-counting.
ids.mechanical-color-pie-2017-2017-06-05: First edition of the recurring mechanical colour pie reference, published 5 June 2017. Rosewater states the intent outright: "I am going to make this a feature I do every few years." The body is the enumeration itself - which colour is primary, secondary or tertiary in each of roughly a hundred effects, running to some 2,700 lines. The transferable craft is entirely in the framing, and all five of those points are already summarized from the 2021 edition: colour identity as a distribution rather than a permission list (primary/secondary/tertiary), the further a colour sits the narrower its door, a rare exception is not part of an identity, publish the state of the system rather than a constitution, and what is written is the centre not the border. The 2017 caveats are the same caveats, almost word for word. mechanical-color-pie-2021 and mechanical-color-pie-2021-changes are the instalments worth keeping; a second summary of the same framing would restate them with older numbers.
ids.eight-hundred-and-counting-2017-05-15: Index of the previous hundred columns, published 15 May 2017 at the 800-week mark - the eighth instalment of the recurring recap series. ids.checking-planeswalkers-2014-06-17: Storyline status directory, published 17 June 2014 and written by Doug Beyer of the creative team rather than Rosewater. It walks every spark-active planeswalker alphabetically - Ajani through Xenagos - and states where each one currently stands: Elspeth in the Theros Underworld, Garruk carrying the Chain Veil curse, Karn hunting Phyrexian corruption. Beyer says outright what it is - a one-stop, up-to-the-minute cheat sheet, Vorthos style - written because the story had scattered across cards, novels, comics, trailers and Duels. It is a reference table of lore facts with no argument about making anything, and the entries share no through-line beyond being characters. Same profile as the other roundups skipped here.
ids.synergy-2014-06-16: Level One, published 16 June 2014 - a different column by a different author, in Mike Flores voice ("Can you see the extra synergy that would have made 1994 Mike Flores so happy?"). It teaches deckbuilding: what synergy is, worked through Kird Ape, two 2006 Worlds RW decklists and their fetchland counts, Bitterblossom in Faeries, and Delver of Secrets needing a third of the deck to be instants and sorceries. It closes by promising a separate instalment on two-card combos. Strategy content sharing the news feed, the same call as one-two-three-times-murder-sideboarding-strategies-and-tactics-part-2.
ids.virtual-card-advantage-2014-06-09: Level One, published 9 June 2014 - a different column by a different author, and the instalment Flores refers back to from synergy-2014-06-16. It is play advice: not-obvious routes to card advantage based on reading opponent behaviour, built on the series own earlier pieces about two-for-ones. Same call as the other Level One columns skipped here.
ids.top-25-rankings-june-12-2014-2014-06-12: Pro rankings bulletin, published 12 June 2014, sharing the news feed rather than a column. It reports that with no major events that week the Magic Top 25 stands unchanged with Reid Duke at the head, then previews the remaining event calendar toward Pro Tour Magic 2015 in Portland. Standings and schedule, no argument about making anything. Same call as the GP Richmond statement and the Magic Online programme update.
ids.touch-magic-2014-06-16: Reader letters, published 16 June 2014. A Blogatog question about coping with anxiety at FNM drew stories back, so Rosewater asked his social media for more, capped them at 200 words, and printed a fraction of what arrived under first names only. The body is entirely other people own words about how Magic changed their lives, running from light to very serious, with Rosewater supplying only the invitation and the thanks. Moving, and no through-line beyond the subject. Judged by the line drawn at celebrity - does the article teach something about making things or receiving them, or is it about being a person - this is testimony rather than argument.
ids.journeys-end-2014-05-26: Storyline recap, published 26 May 2014 by the creative team. It condenses both halves of the Godsend novel - Elspeth arriving on Theros through her final battle with the gods in Nyx - and says so outright: the novel links are given first, and the abbreviated version follows for readers who will not read a novel. Plot summary with no argument about making anything, the same call as checking-planeswalkers-2014-06-17.
ids.life-resource-generally-2014-05-19: Level One, published 19 May 2014 - a different column by a different author, opening on a worked scenario of a player declining to spend a Doom Blade. It is play advice about treating life total as a spendable resource, and it is the instalment the Necropotence piece a week earlier refers back to. Same call as the other Level One columns skipped here.
ids.necropotence-2014-05-12: Level One, published 12 May 2014 - a different column by a different author, and explicitly a continuation: "Over the last couple of weeks, we have talked about the relationship between cards and life total." It reads Necropotence as the card that makes life-into-cards explicit, against Sylvan Library and Greed, then walks period decklists. Card evaluation and play advice rather than design argument, timed to Vintage Masters preview week. Same call as the other Level One columns skipped here.

ids.odds-and-ends-2004-08-23-0: Contest results page rather than a column: twenty-odd reader submissions to a card-name-chaining puzzle, each printed twice (once as the chain, once with the overlapping words expanded), with no surrounding prose and no design content to summarize.
ids.free-association-2004-02-05: Wizards serves only the column's closing questionnaire — ten personal-history questions with Rosewater's own answers (Alpha, a month of misplaying Stasis, trading his father a Fungusaur for a Mox Emerald) — with the column proper absent and no sign-off. All four path variants return the same fragment.
ids.day-life-2003-12-29: Holiday best-of reprint of the February 10, 2003 choose-your-own-adventure column about a day in R&D. Only the framing note survives — the branching body ran on cookie-driven navigation the current site no longer serves, and Rosewater notes it is physically impossible to see everything in one pass. Worth recording for one line from an unnamed R&D member: "It is more realistic than the audience will ever believe."
ids.rules-game-2003-12-22: Holiday best-of reprint of the April 7, 2003 column of the same name, which is summarized separately as rules-game-2003-04-07. Only the new framing differs: he picked it as the year's "good for you" choice and calls it the most important column of the year for anyone interested in Magic design.
ids.type-1-take-2-2003-12-15: Annotated reprint of Playing to Type 1 (2002-07-15), which is summarized separately. Rosewater interleaves the 2002 text with new 2003 commentary and distinguishes them only by colour — black for the old column, green for the new — and the current site strips that markup, so the served text gives no way to tell which sentences are the revisit.
ids.day-life-2003-02-10: Interactive "Choose Your Own Adventure" column whose branching pages are gone. The served article is only the six-paragraph framing intro ("your web browser has to have the ability to accept cookies") and ends at "Welcome to R&D." with no content and no sign-off. Nothing to summarize.
ids.when-cards-go-bad-2002-12-23-0: Best Of Week reprint of "When Cards Go Bad" (2002-01-28), which Rosewater picked as his favourite column of the year. Only the short reprint framing is new; the body is identical. Summarized under the original id and URL instead.
ids.teapot-2002-12-16-0: Duplicate of teapot-2002-12-16 — the same Tempest Week card-by-card design column served at a second URL with one paragraph fewer. Summarized under the fuller variant.
ids.mistakes-ive-made-few-2002-11-11-0: Duplicate of mistakes-ive-made-few-2002-11-11 — the same column served at a second URL with identical content. Summarized under the primary variant.
ids.infinity-and-beyond-2002-11-04-0: Duplicate of infinity-and-beyond-2002-11-04 — the same Mana Engine Week column served at a second URL, three paragraphs shorter. Summarized under the fuller variant.
ids.take-job-and-love-it-2002-10-28-0: Duplicate URL variant of take-job-and-love-it-2002-10-28; the suffixed page serves 31 paragraphs against the unsuffixed page 35. Summarized under the fuller unsuffixed id.
ids.wait-theres-morph-2002-09-09-0: Duplicate URL variant of wait-theres-morph-2002-09-09; both serve the same 28-paragraph column. Summarized under the unsuffixed id.
